headline: A 2019 law temporarily extends several Medicaid and health programs and sets a Medicare payment rule for certain new drugs.
what_it_does: The law extends a Medicaid demonstration program for certified community behavioral health clinics and extends Medicaid spousal protections for people receiving home- and community-based services. It adds fiscal year 2019 funding for the Money Follows the Person program, which helps states shift long-term care from institutions toward home and community settings. It also extends the Family-to-Family Health Information Centers program, which funds family-run groups that support families of children with special health care needs. Finally, it gives statutory authority to a Medicare payment method for new drugs and biologics that adds up to 3% to a wholesale acquisition cost-based payment when average sales price is unavailable.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep participating in the certified clinic Medicaid demonstration program for a temporary period set by the law.

who_it_affects.group: Medicaid recipients receiving home- and community-based services
who_it_affects.how: Spousal impoverishment protections that limit how a spouse's income and assets are counted are extended temporarily.
They receive additional fiscal year 2019 funding and grant opportunities under the Money Follows the Person program.

who_it_affects.group: Families of children with special health care needs
who_it_affects.how: The Family-to-Family Health Information Centers program continues to offer information and peer support through family-run groups.
They remain eligible for federal grants under the Family-to-Family Health Information Centers program for a temporary period.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare providers that furnish new drugs or biologics
who_it_affects.how: They can receive a payment add-on of up to 3% over wholesale acquisition cost when average sales price data is unavailable, for drugs furnished on or after January 1, 2019.

when_it_takes_effect: Provisions generally took effect upon enactment on August 6, 2019, with some changes applying retroactively to January 1, 2019; the extension periods are temporary and set by the bill's text.
